title: GPU burst hiring vs price experiment — Jan 2027 sandbox
content:
Context and objective:

Quick experiment to quantify tradeoffs between provisioning small reserved GPU pools + short-term contractor hiring vs. increasing price floors (per-token or per-route) to control burst costs. This is a working spreadsheet-style note — rough numbers and heuristics, not final proforma.

Summary outcome (short):
- If price-per-1M-tokens increases by 15%, we can avoid hiring ~3 contractors for peak weeks and keep margin within 1.5pp of baseline.
- If we want to preserve developer SLAs (p95 latency targets) and avoid degrade fallback routing, need a minimum burst reserve of 8 GPUs (A100 equiv) or three-week contractor pool (~3 FTE-equivalent) during high season.

Assumptions (callouts):
- Baseline hosted token price (internal cost) = $28 / 1M tokens (after infra + amortized headcount).
- Customer-facing price floor currently modeled at $35 / 1M tokens in staging scenarios.
- A100h cost (cloud list + ops) assumed $3.25 / GPU-hour fully loaded (includes spot reliability, networking, management overhead).
- A contractor (infra ops) to stand up/teardown and manage burst capacity = $9k/week (contract pool overhead, training, shift costs).
- One A100 can sustain ~220k tokens/min for continuous generation mix used in peak workload mix (short chats + few long-form kernels).
- Latency SLO penalty approximated as 0.8% revenue loss per 2x latency degradation for top-tier customers.

Scenario table (monthlyized, round numbers):

| Scenario        | Reserved GPUs | Temp hires (FTE-eq) | Price / 1M tokens ($) | Est. monthly infra cost ($) | Est. monthly total cost ($) | Notes |
|-----------------|----------------|---------------------|------------------------|-----------------------------|------------------------------|-------|
| Baseline        | 4              | 0                   | 35                     | 29,520 (4 * 24h * 30d * 3.25)| 29,520                       | Keep SLA, assume steady load |
| Burst + Contractors | 8          | 3                   | 35                     | 59,040                      | 59,040 + 36,000 contractor (~95k)| Used only 20% of month on average (monthlyized above assumes full-month reserve; see note) |
| Price Lift (15%)| 4              | 0                   | 40.25                  | 29,520                      | 29,520 (infra)               | Revenue increases; some demand elasticity expected (~ -6% token volume) |
| Hybrid (4 GPUs base + 4 burst elastic) | 4 | 1 (on-call) | 37                     | 44,280 (assume burst active 10 days) | 44,280 + 12,000 contract (~56k) | Elastic burst autoscaling policy; ops overhead reduced |

Quick sensitivity (price vs hires to maintain margin target):
- Target margin buffer = 22% (post infra).
- If tokens fall by elasticity 0.06 per 1 (6% per 1% price? approximate), then a 15% price lift reduces volume ~ -6% overall (conservative).
- Hiring cost (3 contractors) monthly equivalent = 36k. Breakeven price uplift required to cover 36k at current revenue run-rate (~$1.2M token revenue/mo) is ~3% price uplift. But UX risk and demand elasticity complicate.

Headcount / hiring plan (short term burst ops):
- Contractor pool (3 people): 2 infra ops (12h staggered shifts), 1 SRE/triage. 6–8 week engagements. Cost est: $9k/week/pool (~$36k/mo if used full month).
- Backfill vs overtime: prefer contractors over full-time hires unless burst > 6 months. If expected bursts recur across > 2 quarters, convert 2 contractors to perm hires (salary + benefits ~ $180k each annualized).

Budget lines (for finance ledger):
- INF-GPU-RESERVE-01: Reserved GPU hours (monthly forecast) = $59,040 (8 GPUs full-month)
- INF-CONTRACT-BURST-01: Contractor pool (temp) = $36,000 / mo (3 contractors)
- INF-TOOLING-01: Burst orchestration automation work = one-off $18,500 (engineering effort + runbook)
- REVENUE-ADJ-01: Modeled price uplift scenario = +15% on selected routes (applied to 40% of token volume)

Micro-sim (sketch):
- If we raise price on premium routes by +15% and selectively apply to 40% token volume, monthly uplift = approx $1.2M * 0.4 * 0.15 = $72k (gross). Elasticity reduces tokens ~ -6% => net uplift ~ $67.7k. That pays for ~1.9 contractors. So raising price partly funds short-term ops but not full pool.

Open tradeoffs / questions:
- Customer Tolerance: Are premium customers tolerant of discrete route uplift? Heavy enterprise customers may pushback even if we offer canary/beta. Need legal + sales alignment before route-level price experiments.
- Operational risk: Contractor-run burst increases human error risk; we should quantify SLO violation risk and insurance buffer.
- Automation runway: One-off tooling cost ($18.5k) likely pays back within 2 months if it halves contractor run-time. Prioritize minimal runbook automation.
- Accounting: How to treat short-term contractor vs reserved GPU budget on P&L vs capex? Finance suggests expense line vs capitalized infra. Confirm with FP&A.

Recommended next steps (quick):
1) Run a 6-week pilot with hybrid configuration: keep 4 GPUs baseline reserved, add automated elastic pool with cloud burst (4 GPUs) triggered by queue depth; staff with 1 contractor on-call + SRE weekly support.
2) Implement price uplift on a small test cohort (5 customers) on non-critical routes for 4 weeks and track token volume, cancellations, and enterprise feedback.
3) Build minimal automation (INF-TOOLING-01) to handle burst scaling, capacity tear-down, and billing tagging (scope: 3 sprints).
4) Re-run sensitivity sheet with actual pilot metrics (token churn, infra hours used, ops hours logged) and produce a final proforma for exec decision.

Quick action items (owners + ETA):
- Finance: model demand elasticity using historical token-volume response to Q3 price test (Liam) — due 2027-01-17.
- SRE/Product: scope INF-TOOLING-01 and provide rough estimate on automation ROI (Owen) — due 2027-01-14.
- Sales/RevOps: identify 5 pilot customers for price uplift (Priya + Sara) — due 2027-01-20.

Notes to self / scratch:
- If pilots show >20% token churn on premium cohort, abort price uplift and prioritize automation + contractor pool.
- Consider offering time-limited burst credits to enterprise customers instead of unilateral price lift to reduce churn risk.

Raw numbers appendix (clipboard-friendly):
- A100 fully loaded: $3.25 / hour
- 1 month ~ 720 hours
- Cost per GPU per month ~ 2340 ($3.25 * 720) -> 4 GPUs = 9,360; 8 GPUs = 18,720 (note earlier we used 29k because included extra ops & redundancy; reconcile before final proforma)
- Contractor cost: $9k / week / pool (3-person pool) -> $36k / month full usage

Bottom line: small price uplifts fund a portion of short-term burst ops but not all. Best combined approach = modest price lift on non-critical routes + automation to reduce contractor time + hybrid reserved+elastic GPU pool to protect latency SLOs.

Unresolved items (for FP&A):
- Exact treatment of one-off automation cost in monthly cadence; amortization period recommended = 3 months.
- Mapping of route-level price application to billing system tags (is tagging reliable?).

-- end --
